headline: The co-op gap on the capture spine closes — a two-hand defusal game lands as the spine's fifth title
lede: The PLAICRAFT plan named a simultaneous two-hand co-op title five stages ago, but only four titles ever reached the shelf. This session built the missing one: three bombs, two seats, and a law where both hands must press inside the same window or the step fails — with a CPU partner inside the seeded sim so solo phones still play it. It shipped as the capture spine's fifth replayable title, and it hashes integers only, so its recorded takes can't drift the way replay verification complained about earlier this week.

notes.text: BOMB DEFUSE (#1811, squash 8caca1d, Part of #1711 / Closes #1800): SYNC/CUT/VENT steps, a VENT gauge where one seat pins the bar while the other seats the needle, and mistakes paid in SECONDS off a fuse ledger (nick -2, strike -4, surge -6) instead of lives — the theme is the timer. All audio synthesized, ~20-word coaching voice, deterministic audit 53/53 with a proven mutant, real-key drive 10/10.

Penalties got redesigned mid-session by the harness itself: the blind contract-check pad pattern must survive 600 ticks on any game, and strikes-on-wrong-wire killed the run before the audit could finish. The fix was also the better rule — a nick that costs two seconds makes the last bomb tense in a way an instant strike never does. Provable constraints made the game, not just permitted it.

Spine wiring landed whole this time — replay drivers + two verified synth sessions, browser loop capture, contract roster, nightly bot roster, and the audit parked in the ciscope scope (adding a check without its scope line is how static goes red). QA polish backlog filed as its own issue (10 gaps) so the QA lane owns it; the phone-hardware stage of the plan stays gated on the storage-bucket question waiting for its answer Nov 8.
